title: Outstation and Courses at Hotels: How to Stay on Track When You're Away from Home?
intro: You don't need to take a 'diet holiday' every time you go outstation or attend a course. With a few small choices at the buffet and coffee break, your progress can stay steady.

sections.p: Walk one round first before taking any food. Start with eggs, chicken or fish, then add the carb you like most. Pick just one, for example nasi lemak or bread, not both. Pastries and cake are fine, but take one small piece.

Coffee breaks usually have kuih, sandwiches and teh tarik. One kuih is an estimated 100-200 calories, so two breaks a day can add up to more than 500 calories. Pick one item you really want, and drink less-sweet tea or coffee.
Use the plate formula: half vegetables, a quarter protein, a quarter rice or noodles. Take dessert in a small portion. Sit a bit further from the buffet table so it's not so easy to go for seconds.

sections.h: Keep moving even without a gym
sections.p: Take the stairs to your room if you can. Walk 15-20 minutes around the hotel in the morning or after the course. In your room, do squats, lunges and wall push-ups for 10 minutes.
Eating out as a group is fun. Order food you enjoy, but share the fried dishes and choose plain water or less-sweet teh o ais limau. You don't have to turn down every invitation.

action: Bring your own water bottle and refill it at every session.
Pick only one sweet item at each coffee break.
Walk 15 minutes every evening after the course sessions.
Bring a small snack like nuts or fruit for the journey.
Sleep at around the same time even when you're at the hotel.
myth: Many people think one week outstation will ruin all their progress. Actually, a 1-2 kg gain after outstation is usually water and salt, and it normally goes down again once your routine is back.

faq.q: The hotel has no gym, what do I do?
faq.a: A 10-15 minute workout in your room is enough. Squats, lunges, planks and push-ups need no equipment at all. Add a walk outside if the area is safe.

faq.q: Do I need to weigh myself while outstation?
faq.a: No need. Your weight will go up and down because of salty food and less sleep. Weigh yourself again 2-3 days after you're back to your usual routine.

faq.q: I feel shy to refuse food when people offer. What should I do?
faq.a: You can take a little and enjoy it. Say thank you and say 'I'm already full' with a smile. Taking a small portion is enough to respect the person offering.
